morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with the inflorescence architecture and pistillate bracts: annual Acalypha with axillary staminate spikes and terminal/short-lateral pistillate spikes; normal pistillate bracts are loosely arranged and deeply divided into narrow lobes.
diagnostic_traits: annual herb, usually low to ~75 cm
alternate ovate serrate leaves, often 3–5-nerved from base
staminate and pistillate inflorescences separated in position
pistillate bracts loosely spaced with narrow lobes

confusers.separator: perennial, terminal bisexual spikes with conspicuous red styles and broader toothed pistillate bracts.
perennial and often functionally dioecious; deeply divided foliage/bracts need comparison.
